key_insight: The paper asks whether DiffusionGemma is less transparent because it computes more in a continuous latent space, and separates transparency into what we can see in intermediate states versus whether we can infer the underlying algorithm. The core idea is that transparency is not one-dimensional, and diffusion-style reasoning can be evaluated more precisely than simply saying it is "more" or "less" transparent.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of understanding and measuring reasoning transparency in LLMs that operate through continuous latent diffusion rather than discrete token-by-token computation.
method: Decompose transparency into two parts: variable transparency (can we interpret intermediate snapshots?) and algorithmic transparency (can we infer the computation strategy?).
Analyze DiffusionGemma’s intermediate latent states to see how interpretable the model’s internal reasoning steps are.
Compare transparency properties against more traditional LLM reasoning behavior to determine whether continuous computation changes interpretability.
impact: This helps researchers and practitioners judge whether diffusion-based language models are easier or harder to debug, audit, and align. It also provides a clearer framework for evaluating model reasoning transparency beyond standard token-based assumptions.
visual_elements: A split-axis diagram showing variable transparency vs. algorithmic transparency.
A side-by-side comparison of discrete token reasoning and continuous latent diffusion.
A pipeline graphic of DiffusionGemma intermediate snapshots over time.
Icons for debugging, safety, and interpretability to connect transparency to practical use cases.
paper_authors: Joshua Engels, Callum McDougall, Bilal Chughtai, Janos Kramar, Senthoran Rajamanoharan
